lines.text: Stare at the cross in the middle. Don't move your eyes.
Keep staring. The colours around it start to fade.
Some might vanish completely, leaving just grey.
This is called Troxler fading. It was first described by a Swiss doctor in 1804.
Your neurons stop responding to things that don't change.
If something in your side vision stays perfectly still and blurry, your brain decides it's not worth reporting.
Move your eyes even a little, and it all comes back.
Your brain is constantly deleting things it thinks you don't need to see.

sources.claim: Troxler's fading: described by Ignaz Troxler in 1804; a steady, blurred peripheral stimulus fades during fixation due to neural adaptation
